Find the terms that distinguish groups of nodes (tf-idf)

Source: R/extract_tfidf.R
extract_tfidf.Rd

Clusters are defined by the structure of the network, not by the content of the nodes. To interpret them, it helps to know which words are specific to each cluster. extract_tfidf() extracts the words and n-grams of one or several text columns (e.g. titles, abstracts) and returns, for each group (e.g. each cluster), the terms with the highest tf-idf (Spärck Jones 1972; Salton and Buckley 1988) : $$\mathrm{tf}_{td} = \frac{n_{td}}{\sum_u n_{ud}}, \qquad \mathrm{idf}_t = \log\frac{D}{\mathrm{df}_t}, \qquad \text{tf-idf}_{td} = \mathrm{tf}_{td} \times \mathrm{idf}_t,$$ with \(n_{td}\) the count of term \(t\) in group \(d\), \(D\) the number of groups and \(\mathrm{df}_t\) the number of groups containing \(t\). A term present in every group has a tf-idf of 0.

Usage

extract_tfidf(
  data,
  text_columns,
  grouping_columns,
  grouping_across_list = FALSE,
  n_gram = 2L,
  stopwords_type = "smart",
  stopwords_vector = NULL,
  clean_word_method = c("lemmatize", "stemming", "none"),
  ngrams_filter = 5L,
  nb_terms = 5L
)

Arguments

data

A tbl_graph, a list of tbl_graphs (their node tables are stacked) or a data frame.

text_columns

Character vector, the column(s) with text. Several columns are pasted together, separated by ". ".

grouping_columns

Character vector, the column(s) defining the groups, the "documents" of the tf-idf (e.g. "cluster_leiden").

grouping_across_list

Logical. For a list of graphs whose group identifiers repeat across graphs (cluster "01" exists in every window), TRUE adds the name of the graph to the groups, so that each cluster of each window is a separate document. Not needed for identifiers that are already unique across the list, such as dynamic clusters.

n_gram

Integer, the maximum length of n-grams (2 by default: words and pairs of words).

stopwords_type

Character scalar, the stop word list of tidytext::get_stopwords() ("smart" by default).

stopwords_vector

Optional character vector of stop words, used instead of stopwords_type.

clean_word_method

"lemmatize", "stemming" (with the textstem package) or "none" (chosen when no method is given).

ngrams_filter

Integer, the minimum number of occurrences of a term in the whole corpus (5 by default).

nb_terms

Integer, the number of terms returned per group (5 by default).

Value

A data.table with one row per group and term, for the nb_terms best terms of each group: the grouping columns, term, n (count of the term in the group), tf, idf and tf_idf.

Details

The texts are lower-cased and split into n-grams of 1 to n_gram words by tidytext::unnest_tokens() (Silge and Robinson 2017) . Each word is lemmatised or stemmed if requested; n-grams containing a stop word or a number are dropped, as are terms rarer than ngrams_filter in the corpus and terms appearing only once in a group, which would otherwise reach the top of small groups by accident.

The choice of the groups decides what "specific" means: computed on the clusters of one network, tf-idf finds what distinguishes a cluster from the other clusters of the same period; computed on the stacked windows with grouping_across_list = TRUE, it also distinguishes a cluster from its own past and future.

Lemmatising and stemming are optional and need the textstem package. For larger corpora or other weighting schemes, the text-mining functions of the mintR package (https://codeberg.org/agoutsmedt/mintR) can be used on the node table.

References

Salton G, Buckley C (1988). “Term-Weighting Approaches in Automatic Text Retrieval.” Information Processing & Management, 24(5), 513–523.

Silge J, Robinson D (2017). Text Mining with R: A Tidy Approach. O'Reilly.

Spärck Jones K (1972). “A Statistical Interpretation of Term Specificity and Its Application in Retrieval.” Journal of Documentation, 28(1), 11–21.

Examples

network <- build_network(
  nodes = subset(Nodes_stagflation, source_type == "Stagflation"),
  directed_edges = Ref_stagflation,
  source_id = "source_id",
  target_id = "target_id",
  projection_method = "structured",
  cooccurrence_method = "coupling_similarity",
  edges_threshold = 1
)
network <- add_clusters(
  network,
  clustering_method = "leiden",
  objective_function = "modularity",
  seed = 123,
  verbose = FALSE
)

extract_tfidf(
  network,
  text_columns = "source_title",
  grouping_columns = "cluster_leiden",
  n_gram = 2,
  clean_word_method = "none",
  nb_terms = 3
)
